This 
document details the steps required to check the nitrogen pressure for
SF6 Switchgear (Siemens type 8D.4/220kv)

items:
A work permit must be issued, 
the qualified maintenance staff should
 carry the suitable safety category,

Safety fence (rope) with caution 
marks surrounding the work area,
Wear your safety helmet, shoes .... etc

sections.text:
Note: Refer to diagrams and pictures in Siemens Instruction Manual No. (SW 8518a) or
 (SW 8364-220)
 The nitrogen pressure is the priming pressure of the "stored energy"
 accumulator, it is factory set and should be approx. 200 bars at an ambient
 temperature of +20oC

During the measuring procedure the oil pressure will be reduced to zero and
 the breaker will be in "lock-out" mode.

items: Measure and record the ambient temperature inside the GIS building.

Switch off the oil pump by tripping magnetic circuit breaker (F201) inside
 the control panel.

Unscrew the locking screw (14.39) inside the control panel.(5mm allen key
 required)

Using a 13mm special pipe socket with "T" handle, carefully and
 slowly open the pressure equalizing valve (14.37).

Observe the hydraulic oil pressure gauge very closely. At first the
 pressure will decrease very slowly from 320 bars to a certain value, then
 the pressure will suddenly drop to zero. The nitrogen priming pressure can
 be recorded at the intermediate point, when the pressure suddenly begins to
 drop. Under normal conditions the priming pressure should be 200 bars at +
 20 C.

Substations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This 
document details the steps required to check the nitrogen pressure for
SF6 Switchgear (Siemens type 8D.4/220kv)
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued, 
the qualified maintenance staff should
 carry the suitable safety category,
Safety fence (rope) with caution 
marks surrounding the work area,
Wear your safety helmet, shoes .... etc
Breaker must be isolated.
Work to be carried out
Note: Refer to diagrams and pictures in Siemens Instruction Manual No. (SW 8518a) or
 (SW 8364-220)
 The nitrogen pressure is the priming pressure of the "stored energy"
 accumulator, it is factory set and should be approx. 200 bars at an ambient
 temperature of +20oC
During the measuring procedure the oil pressure will be reduced to zero and
 the breaker will be in "lock-out" mode.
Measure and record the ambient temperature inside the GIS building.
Switch off the oil pump by tripping magnetic circuit breaker (F201) inside
 the control panel.
Unscrew the locking screw (14.39) inside the control panel.(5mm allen key
 required)
Using a 13mm special pipe socket with "T" handle, carefully and
 slowly open the pressure equalizing valve (14.37).
Observe the hydraulic oil pressure gauge very closely. At first the
 pressure will decrease very slowly from 320 bars to a certain value, then
 the pressure will suddenly drop to zero. The nitrogen priming pressure can
 be recorded at the intermediate point, when the pressure suddenly begins to
 drop. Under normal conditions the priming pressure should be 200 bars at +
 20 C.
Note: The pressure will vary according to ambient temperature as indicated in the
 table below.
Record Hydraulic Alarm/Lock-Out pressure as per table below
On Decreasing pressure | On Increasing Pressure
Pump Stock | ____________ bar
Auto Reclose Lock-Out ____________bar | ____________ bar
On Lock-Out ____________ bar | ____________ bar
General Lock-Out ____________ bar | ____________ bar
Close the pressure-equalizing valve.
Carefully re-tighten the locking screw.
Switch on the oil pump and carefully observe the hydraulic pressure gauge.
 The pressure should rapidly climb to a certain value (priming pressure),
 note and record this pressure. The pressure will then slowly increase to
 full system pressure of approx. 320 bars.
Compare the two readings in step 5 and in step 8
Record Hydraulic Alarm/Lock-Out pressure as per table below
